claims.text: The as-synthesized PGM nanoscale catalyst has a native, partially oxidized surface containing a submonolayer oxide/hydroxide.
A dynamic submonolayer surface oxide/hydroxide governs the catalyst's performance in ethanol oxidation.
The submonolayer oxide/hydroxide tunes the electronic structure of the active PGM sites.
The surface oxide/hydroxide facilitates adsorption and activation of ethanol and reaction intermediates.
The surface oxide/hydroxide enables complete 12-electron oxidation of ethanol.
The surface oxide/hydroxide resists catalyst deactivation.
A mild hydrogen reduction treatment can selectively remove or reduce the submonolayer surface oxide/hydroxide.
The submonolayer oxide/hydroxide modulates the d-band center of the PGM.
The submonolayer oxide/hydroxide adjusts the binding energies of ethanol and intermediate species.
Adjusted adsorbate binding suppresses catalyst poisoning.
Removing the oxide/hydroxide disrupts the proposed electronic properties and changes adsorption/desorption kinetics.
Catalysts retaining the native submonolayer oxide/hydroxide will exhibit high ethanol-oxidation activity, selectivity, and durability.
Removing the surface oxide/hydroxide will lower ethanol-oxidation reaction rates.
Removing the surface oxide/hydroxide will alter product selectivity.
Removing the surface oxide/hydroxide will reduce durability during ethanol oxidation.
The proposed oxide-mediated effect applies under moderate-temperature, acidic, dynamically cycled fuel-cell conditions.
Strongly reducing conditions remove the surface oxide/hydroxide and may change the proposed behavior.
Highly oxidizing conditions produce thick oxide layers and may change the proposed behavior.

contradictions.description: The prediction says reduction will produce altered selectivity, whereas the falsification rule requires a statistically significant decrease in selectivity. An alteration could be an increase, a decrease, or merely a product-distribution shift, so the decisive criterion is not fully aligned with the prediction.
